assessments.task_description:
A series of quizzes are associated with weekly online modules. You need to complete the weekly learning materials before taking the associated quiz. The quizzes are to be completed online and some have practice (formative) quizzes that can be attempted multiple times.

The quiz each week is based on the learning materials from the prior week. The Week 1 quiz is based on assumed knowledge of insects orders. There are pre-course learning materials available on Blackboard for those wanting a refresher or who are learning insect identification and classification for the first time.

Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT)

Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT) are emerging tools that may support students in completing this assessment task. Students must NOT use AI and/or MT in completing this assessment task. Using AI or MT for these assessment tasks may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct.
assessments.submission_guidelines: Completed online via the course website in Learn.UQ
assessments.deferral_or_extension: You may be able to apply for an extension.
assessments.late_submission: A penalty of 10% of the maximum possible mark will be deducted per 24 hours from time submission is due for up to 7 days. After 7 days, you will receive a mark of 0.
assessments.additional_info: You may be able to apply for an extension.

assessments.task_description:
Identify insects to family, genus or species as specified. You will be required to demonstrate successful use of identification tools, which may include textbooks, dichotomous keys, LUCID keys and/or guidebooks.

To be held during the tutorial time slot. This is a check-point quiz to make sure you are on track with using identification tools.

Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT)

Students should NOT use AI and/or MT in completing this assessment task.
assessments.submission_guidelines: You will be provided the quiz on Blackboard during the class tutorial.
assessments.deferral_or_extension: You may be able to defer this exam.
assessments.late_submission: Exams submitted after the end of the submission time will incur a late penalty.
assessments.additional_info: You may be able to defer this exam.

assessments.task_description:
You need to make and submit a physical or digital insect collection, or a combination of physical and digital collection. The full criteria are available on Blackboard.

Important: Students are advised to ensure that they have the appropriate permission/permits for wherever they intend to collect. Note that it is very difficult to obtain permits to collect insects in QLD. Even local parks and bushland are out-of-bounds.

If you do not have a backyard or other private property, we advise that you attend the optional field trip to obtain insects from Hidden Vale. If you are making a digital collection, you do not need a permit from public land if you are not taking insects. You will, however, need a good camera with macro capability.

Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT)

Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT) are emerging tools that may support students in completing this assessment task. Students may appropriately use AI and/or MT in completing this assessment task. Students must clearly reference any use of AI or MT in each instance. A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct.
assessments.submission_guidelines: Physical insect collections are to be handed in during class times in Week 7 or posted to UQ with a receipt by the due date and time. Digital collections are to be submitted via the Turnitin link that will appear in the Assessments menu, by the due date and time. Note that you cannot post insects into Australia. If you are not in Australia, you must do a digital collection.
assessments.deferral_or_extension: You may be able to apply for an extension.
assessments.late_submission: A penalty of 10% of the maximum possible mark will be deducted per 24 hours from time submission is due for up to 7 days. After 7 days, you will receive a mark of 0.
assessments.additional_info: You may be able to apply for an extension.

assessments.task_description:
The oral assessment will be one-on-one with the course coordinator. It will include specimens that you need to identify to family, genus or species using the specified resources. You will be required to demonstrate competent use of identification tools, including specific multiple entry and dichotomous keys.

You can choose whether to do the oral assessment in person or via zoom with your video on. You will be able to choose your own time slot, with options starting from 25 January 2027. If you cannot attend the scheduled interview, please contact the course coordinator for alternative dates.

You need to pass this assessment in order to pass the course.

Questions may specify particular resources that must be used but might also include a question where Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Translation (MT) can optionally be used. All approaches must be acknowledged as they are being used in the oral exam. A failure to reference/mention any resources used might constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct.

The oral assessment will be recorded.
